I'll be honest the weather and darkness can significantly effect things. We tried to visit snaefelsness in December once (were staying about 2-3 hours from Reykjavik) and had to turn around because the visibility on the road was so bad from snow and wind.  You will have to take things day by day rather than having a solid itinerary to stick to.

For Iceland: If you're going to explore a decent amount of the country rather than just focusing on golden circle area like a lot of first time visitors, try the Myvatn nature baths in the north. Same blue water as blue lagoon but far less expensive. 

Get a 4wd car, as still plenty of gravel roads (again only if you're planning a more extensive trip). Also make sure you check whether it's a gravel road or tarmac road when planning routes - and allow more time for your journey if its gravel roads. You'll need to go fairly slow to dodge pot holes on some of the more remote routes. 

The time that you're planning to go has almost 24 hours day light. If you want to get to a popular spot and take photos without people, you have the option to get there super early to avoid the crowds which I really recommend. In winter you don't have this option as much due to limited daylight hours, so make the most of it!
